title: Chapter 10. Caste and Lineage
html:
The right to the Name comes from faith, not birth; pride of lineage leads to enmity toward devotion; a cobbler devotee is higher than a brahmana without devotion; humility and the mercy of Nityananda (pp. 28–29)

[p. 28]

1Having gained faith, every human being is entitled to the Name:
arguments and bragging about caste and lineage have no place here.

2The noble lineage of a brahmana does not make one fit for bhajana;
one of low caste who has faith is not unfit for bhajana.

3In the ten worldly rites caste and lineage hold sway;1
in the service of Krishna caste and lineage carry no weight.

4The proud man, puffed up with caste and lineage,
is hostile to devotion and goes to the abode of hell.

5He honours neither Vaishnavas nor devotees, nor heeds right and wrong;
out of pride he always does what is lawless and forbidden.

6One who is a cobbler and serves Krishna gains Krishna's mercy;
one who is pure [by birth] but without devotion gets no mercy from Krishna.

7Though a brahmana be adorned with twelve qualities,
without devotion to Krishna he goes away to hell.2

8Where there is devotion to Krishna, there are all good qualities:
of their own accord they dwell in that person always.

[p. 29]

9Ornaments on a corpse are repulsive;
the japa and austerity of a non-devotee are mere outward riches.

10Serve, brother, with all your heart the son of Shachi,
and pride in caste and lineage will be cast away.

11Give up pride, brother, and you will give up worldliness;
give up worldliness, and your heart will be purified.

12Withdrawing attachment from worldly things,
lovingly devote yourself to Krishna's lotus feet.

13Though you be of noble lineage — what harm is there in that?
Give up pride in lineage and be humble of mind.

14Bhagavan is especially merciful to the humble:
pride and humility do not dwell in one place.

15Pride is the road to hell: carefully give it up;
in humility immerse yourself in the lotus feet of Radha and Govinda.

16Ah, when will Prabhu Nityananda be merciful to me,
free me from pride and give me the shade of His feet?

Notes

  1. The ten purificatory rites (samskaras) of a householder's life — from conception to marriage and so on.
  2. Cf. Bhagavatam 7.9.10: a brahmana with twelve qualities but averse to the Lord's lotus feet is lower than a chandala devotee; the verse is quoted in CC Madhya 20.
